tw-ia-tiffin-booty-diagram-1903.st: The Iowa City Press-Citizen (16 Oct 1903) says 'half the town' searched, and that the digger was said to be after valuables stolen from the unknown man found murdered in the Ackerman timber near Oxford a few years earlier; that timber is the murder site, not the cache. An Illinois penitentiary convict gave him the plot, and Sheriff Hofer and a deputy were hunting him.
src: Iowa City Press-Citizen, 16 Oct 1903, p. 9, "Seeks Treasure" (Newspapers.com 8658756)

set.pl: Enes (ex-Ritter?) brewery at the bluff foot, ~0.8 km S of downtown Henderson, W side of the bluff-toe road (1894/1910 Sanborns); hillside tunnel behind
set.t: Found and dug out; look-only. The 1894 Sanborn map (sheet 1) shows the Jno. Enes Brewery about 1/2 mile south of the post office, built against the hill beside the road up the bluff, with ice houses and a malt house; it is the only brewery on the 1894 and 1910 Sanborns, so the pin is on it; that it was Ritter's earlier plant is an inference. In 1926 the site was called the old Ritter brewery ruins; whether it is the 'Jno. Enes Brewery' of the 1894 Sanborn is unconfirmed (Enes may have been Ritter's successor). The 1880 census confirms an Enes brewery: John Enes, 53, and Christian Enes, 25, brewers, alongside Joseph Ritter, 52, and Albert Miller, 27, also brewers, so Henderson had two brewing families.
pinev: LoC Sanborn Henderson 1894 and 1910: "John Enes Brewery, located 1/2 mile S of P.O.", brick brewhouse, malt house and kiln at the foot of a "Vacant High Hill" on the W, drive on the E, "water piped from spring on hill"; the only brewery mapped.
Inference only: the 1880 census lists both Ritter and Enes as brewers, so Ritter's earlier hillside plant (the 1926 'old Ritter brewery ruins') is taken to be this one.

set.pl: Bear River reach south of Petoskey (1913 gravel pit, not yet placed). Wegemer gravel pit (1913): Frank X. Wegemer's pit (the 1913 paper printed 'Franz Z.') on the bank of Bear River, S of the city.
pinev: Detroit News 2 Nov 1913 puts the pit on the bank of Bear River in the southern part of the city (inside Petoskey), and says the Ottawas went a short way up from the mouth near the Pere Marquette station. Pin on the lower river reach in south Petoskey, r1 km. Pin conf D.

1919 Sanborn sheet 18: only a clay pit by the roundhouse on the S bank; no gravel pit; the river S of Grimes/Winfield Sts is unmapped. Owner Frank X. Wegemer, mason/contractor (the Detroit Free Press had 'Franz Z.'). Best area: S bank between Grimes/Winfield Sts and the S city line (~45.358-45.365, -84.955/-84.960), pending a 1910s Emmet plat.
